Sean / Monica — quick legal read: FinTechCo asks that we accept two substantive changes that are not our standard policy: 1) unilateral 30-day deletion requirement and 2) an open-ended subprocessor objection process tied to EEA data.

Proposed approach (recommended):
- Subprocessor notice: agree to 30-day notice for new subprocessors and provide a named subprocessor list in Appendix A; if FinTechCo objects, we will engage in good-faith remediation or offer a short-term mitigation (e.g., routing to a different region) for a 30-day transition. We should resist an unfettered veto — instead offer a defined objection window (e.g., 14 days) and escalation to legal.
- Objection process: add a mechanism for expedited review and an automatic fallback if remediation is not feasible; this avoids a complete bar to services.
- Deletion timelines: counter to 45 days for account-level deletion requests; commit to 30 days for customer data exports/erasure where technically feasible, but keep the 90-day retention for backups and disaster recovery with clear exception language.

I think these are negotiable but require VP Legal exception approval because they deviate from our privacy baseline. If we can get sign-off, we can prepare the final DPA to send via DocuSign.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
